content:
devon: Heads-up — hit a surprising bug when using the async client under concurrency with quota headers. Rapid repro below.

maria: Ugh, details?

devon: Repro steps: 1) create 50 coroutines that call `client.chat.completions.create` concurrently, 2) server replies with quota headers e.g. `x-quota-remaining: 1000`, `x-quota-reset: 1680000000` for each response, 3) client-side merger logic reduces remaining to negative numbers over time.

ryan: Hmm do you mean the local quota cache is being updated non-atomically?

devon: Exactly. Current helper `merge_quota_headers` is pure-sync and does: `cache_remaining = min(cache_remaining, header_remaining)` which races with async tasks. With heavy concurrency you end up double-counting and then triggering false throttles.

anya: Can you paste the header parsing code snippet?

devon: Sure — simplified:
```
def merge_quota_headers(cache, headers):
    rem = int(headers.get("x-quota-remaining", "0"))
    cache["remaining"] = min(cache.get("remaining", rem), rem)
    cache["reset"] = max(cache.get("reset", 0), int(headers.get("x-quota-reset", 0)))
```
When many tasks call this concurrently the `min`/`max` sequence reads stale values and writes back outdated numbers.

maria: That code obviously isn't thread/async safe. We should either use an `asyncio.Lock` around the cache OR refactor to return diffs and apply them centrally in a single writer task.

ryan: For the Python SDK we should also think about typing: an explicit `TokenBucket` public class with typed async methods helps. e.g.
```
class AsyncTokenBucket:
    async def consume(self, tokens: int) -> bool: ...
    async def peek(self) -> int: ...
```
This lets middleware call `await bucket.consume(n)` instead of mutating dicts.

anya: I like returning diffs + central writer pattern. Less lock overhead. Also for sync users we need a parallel `TokenBucket` API so parity is preserved. Maybe provide a `TokenBucketProtocol` with `sync` and `async` impls.

devon: Proposal: 1) add `redwood.rate.AsyncTokenBucket` and `redwood.rate.TokenBucket` classes, 2) export `parse_quota_headers(headers) -> Dict[str,int]` as pure function (no global state), 3) add `RateLimitMiddleware` that accepts a `TokenBucket` instance and updates central bucket via a single background writer task for async flows.

maria: Also the 429 handling: server sends `Retry-After` sometimes with float seconds, sometimes epoch timestamp. We need a robust parser and prefer honoring `x-quota-reset` if present. Small function `parse_retry_after(value)` would be nice.

ryan: Agree. Also typings: use `typing.ParamSpec` for middleware callables to keep mypy happy. And add small sample app under `examples/async_rate` demonstrating heavy concurrency + bucket.

devon: I started a quick branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/999 — it's a draft with the AsyncTokenBucket and tests for concurrent merges. Not ready but shows approach.

sdk-bot: CI started for PR #999 — build queued.

anya: Nice. Can you add a stress test that simulates interleaved header arrival times? That helped catch a subtle case for me.

devon: Yep will add. Also need guidance on API ergonomics: Should `consume` raise on insufficient tokens or return False? I prefer return bool for middleware integration.

maria: Return bool + optional `wait=True` flag that blocks until tokens available (async wait) sounds flexible.

ryan: One more: document the expected header names we rely on (`x-quota-remaining`, `x-quota-reset`, `x-rate-limit`, `retry-after`) in the SDK docs and console so customers know hints.

anya: I'll file an issue to prioritize: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/issues/424 (added) — tagging @maria @ryan for review.

devon: Thanks — will push updated tests and the `examples/async_rate` sample shortly. :rocket:

maria: Thanks for catching this. Small follow-up: please add a changelog entry for the new public classes so downstreams know about the surface change.

ryan: Ack. If anyone hits this urgently, you can workaround by passing `client._http._rate_cache_lock = asyncio.Lock()` in tests, but obviously that's not a real fix.

devon: noted. Will keep the patch minimal and opt-in.

sdk-bot: PR #999 — CI passed on linux/py3.11.

anya: Great, moving to review.
